findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that verifies the LLM contradiction criterion (Approach step 3) flags a present-but-wrong provenance declaration (e.g. attested account 579718921998 vs IaC-named 896586841071), and clarify whether the AC1 regression fixture exercises the DET presence check, the LLM contradiction check, or both.
evidence: Approach step 3: 'Let an LLM criterion judge the declaration against repo facts — ... "plan attests account X, IaC names account Y" becomes a repo-checkable contradiction'
AC1: 'lacking measurement provenance is flagged by a DETERMINISTIC check (no LLM), and the wrong-account escape is reproduced as a regression fixture from the real 579718921998 vs 896586841071 case'
AC2 references 'the new criterion ships advisory' without stating whether it is the DET presence check or the LLM contradiction criterion
findings.finding: Approach step 3 introduces an LLM criterion that judges the provenance *declaration* against repo facts (catching 'plan attests account X, IaC names account Y'), but no acceptance criterion verifies this contradiction-detection behavior. AC1 binds the wrong-account regression fixture to the DETERMINISTIC presence check, yet a presence check only proves fields are non-empty — it cannot detect a provenance block that is present but names the wrong account (579718921998 vs 896586841071). The escape that motivates the epic is a present-but-wrong declaration, which is the LLM criterion's job, leaving that deliverable without a covering criterion.
findings.location: Approach step 3 vs Acceptance Criteria AC1/AC2
scenarios: An operator supplies a provenance block naming account 579718921998 while IaC names 896586841071 — the DET presence check passes (fields present); only the LLM criterion would flag it, but no AC verifies that path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile parent 3147 AC1's regression-fixture clause with the child: either amend the parent AC to route the '579718921998 vs 896586841071' regression fixture to 98df, or bring that fixture (and the rule-(a) firing it proves) into f161's delivered scope.
evidence: Parent AC1: 'an [operator-attested] criterion lacking measurement provenance is flagged by a DETERMINISTIC check (no LLM), AND the wrong-account escape is reproduced as a regression fixture from the real 579718921998 vs 896586841071 case'.

Child Testing lists 'Contradiction detection, contract tier: ... This is the regression test for the actual escape — build the fixture from the real one (579718921998 declared, 896586841071 in infra/terraform/versions.tf).' — but this exercises the AGENT contradiction rule (a).

Child Descope section: rule (a) 'fires on an environment contradiction' is among the six criteria that 'moved to 98df', and 'What it does not deliver is evidence that the LLM half behaves as the rubric specifies.'

98df is status 'idea', parent_id empty, linked only via 'discovered_from' to f161 — it is NOT a sibling in the container roster; its AC table places the '579718921998 ... 896586841071' must-fire fixture inside 98df's own eval corpus.
Sole-child topology: parent states 'Epic 3147 has exactly ONE child (this story), so no sibling can deliver it.'
container pairing: parent + f161-c70a-1a69-4ed1
findings.finding: Parent AC1's second conjunct — 'the wrong-account escape is reproduced as a REGRESSION FIXTURE from the real 579718921998 vs 896586841071 case' — is not delivered by any roster child; it is descoped into idea 98df, which is not a covering sibling and explicitly does not claim it done. The escape is only DETECTED by the AGENT environment-contradiction rule (a), whose runtime behaviour the child moves out.
scenarios: Completion verifier evaluates parent 3147 AC1 and finds the DET-flag half satisfied but no in-repo regression fixture that reproduces the wrong-account escape being CAUGHT, because that fixture lives in an un-started idea (98df).
A reader treats the child's 'Contradiction detection, contract tier' test as satisfying AC1's fixture clause, unaware the child's Descope section withdraws exactly that runtime behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: Split parent AC1 into two AC — (i) the DET no-LLM presence flag (delivered by f161) and (ii) the wrong-account contradiction regression fixture (delivered by 98df) — and cite 98df as the covering child for (ii); or restore the environment-contradiction regression test to f161's In-scope/Testing as an offline fixture rather than a live semantic run.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the promotion mechanism to ADR-0054's dogfood-and-observe (§3b) with a pressure-release/advisory posture for the NEW criterion, since corpus replay over historical sidecars cannot model a criterion whose findings were never in the corpus.
evidence: Plan step 4: 'Land the generalized rule as an advisory criterion per ADR-0054; corpus replay decides promotion.'
ADR-0054 §3(a): replay 'cannot model a change that alters what the verifier emits ... replay yields a bound, not a prediction'
ADR-0054 Consequences: 'the corpus can only tell you about findings the reviewer surfaced. It is silent on defects the reviewer never raised at all'
ADR-0054 §3(b): dogfood-and-observe is 'the ONLY sanctioned way to validate a change replay can only bound'
findings.finding: AC2/step 4 state the advisory criterion's promotion is decided by 'corpus replay' per ADR-0054, but ADR-0054 excludes exactly this: replay 'cannot model a change that alters what the verifier emits' and the corpus is 'silent on defects the reviewer never raised at all' — a brand-new criterion's findings are absent from the historical corpus, so replay cannot predict its fire behavior; ADR-0054's own sanctioned path for such a change is dogfood-and-observe (§3b), not replay.
findings.location: Approach step 4 + Acceptance Criterion 2 ('corpus replay decides promotion')
scenarios: Implementer plans to gate promotion of the new provenance criterion on a corpus-replay delta and finds the historical sidecars never carried this criterion's findings, so replay produces no fire-rate signal for it
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'corpus replay decides promotion' with 'ships advisory (pressure-release) and is validated by ADR-0054 §3(b) dogfood-and-observe on accumulated sidecars', reserving replay for any downstream threshold/impact-model change that is purely a function of the persisted verification payload.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve where the DETERMINISTIC provenance-presence check lives: either (a) accept it in the packaged P6 floor and reconcile AC2's 'shipped defaults unchanged', or (b) specify the net-new .rebar/-overlay-routable AC-text DET seam, since ADR-0016's overlay DET path is a file_impact-scoped code detector that cannot lint AC text.
evidence: Plan step 2: 'Enforce their presence deterministically, zero LLM, mirroring src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py'
Plan AC2: 'rides the .rebar/ project overlay, leaving the shipped default criteria set unchanged for other rebar clients'

det_operator_attested's lint is invoked inside the packaged static floor: det_floor.py:476 `items = det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines(...)` in `p6_ac_quality`; docs/plan-review-gate.md:118 labels it 'P6 family'

ADR-0016 overlay DET criteria are code-smell DETECTORS scoped to file_impact: det_invariants._run_one requires a `detector` selector and returns abstain with 'no_detector_selector' when absent (det_invariants.py:90-98); there is no overlay seam for an AC-text DET lint
findings.finding: Approach step 2 prescribes a DETERMINISTIC presence-check 'mirroring det_operator_attested.py', but that module is an AC-text lint inside the packaged static P6 floor (shipped to all rebar clients), while AC2 requires the criterion to ride the .rebar/ project overlay and leave shipped defaults unchanged; the only DET overlay mechanism (ADR-0016) is a code-detector scoped to file_impact and cannot lint AC checklist text, so the named mechanism and the overlay-scoping requirement are in tension.
scenarios: Child story tries to route the DET presence-check through .rebar/criteria_routing.json as exec:DET and finds it must supply a code detector, which cannot inspect AC checklist text
Child story puts the DET presence-check in the packaged P6 floor to reuse det_operator_attested, thereby changing shipped defaults for all clients and violating AC2
findings.suggested_fix: State in the child story that the DET presence-check is either a packaged P6-floor addition (and adjust AC2 to say the shipped default set changes but the new *judging* criterion is advisory/overlay), or introduce an AC-text DET criterion kind that ADR-0016 does not currently support — do not assume the existing exec:DET overlay path can run an AC-text lint.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before committing the child-story schema, weigh the proposed measurement-provenance fields against SLSA provenance / in-toto predicate vocabulary (which already model environment, principal/builder.id, and completeness) AND rebar's existing in-toto Statement envelopes (ADR-0044); adopt/align the naming where it fits, or record in the ADR (AC3) why a bespoke shape is warranted.
evidence: Plan Approach 1: 'Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields — environment, principal, and privilege posture relative to production.'

Retrieved SLSA provenance predicate (slsa.dev/spec/v0.1/provenance & v0.2): predicate carries `invocation.environment`, `builder.id` (principal-like), and `metadata.completeness{parameters,environment,materials}` — the same three axes (context, identity, what-was-captured) the plan proposes.

Retrieved in-toto Attestation Framework (slsa.dev/blog/2023/05/in-toto-and-slsa): a context-specific Predicate over Subjects — the exact 'declare the measurement context as structured text' shape the plan wants.

In-repo prior art: ADR-0044 substrate 'DSSE is the Sigstore / in-toto / SLSA standard'; the 9109 opcert payload decodes to `_type: https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1` — rebar attestations ALREADY are in-toto Statements, so the provenance vocabulary is in-house, not foreign.

ANTI-repackaging: the plan names ADR-0043 as 'the shape it changes' but nowhere weighs whether the new provenance fields should reuse/align with the SLSA-predicate / in-toto envelope model rebar already ships.
findings.finding: The plan invents a 'measurement-provenance' evidence contract (environment / principal / privilege-posture-relative-to-production, plus a declaration of what the measurement could observe) without considering the on-point prior art it repackages: SLSA/in-toto provenance predicates already model exactly these axes (`environment`, `invocation`/`builder.id` principal, `completeness` flags), and rebar's OWN attestation substrate is already in-toto Statements over DSSE (ADR-0044). The child-story schema risks reinventing a provenance vocabulary the project already uses.
findings.location: Approach step 1 ('Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields — environment, principal, and privilege posture relative to production') and AC3 ('an ADR records the amended evidence contract, citing ADR-0043')
scenarios: The child story defines a bespoke provenance field set that diverges from (and cannot interoperate with) the in-toto Statement envelopes rebar already emits for plan-review/completion opcerts.
A future consumer wanting to correlate measurement provenance with the signed opcert finds two incompatible provenance schemas.
findings.suggested_fix: In AC3's ADR, add a short 'prior art' subsection: map the three provenance fields to their SLSA/in-toto analogues (environment→`invocation.environment`, principal→`builder.id`, privilege-posture / observability→a `completeness`-style declared-scope flag), and state explicitly whether the amended `[operator-attested]` contract reuses that vocabulary or intentionally diverges (and why the LLM-judges-declaration-against-repo-facts step is the genuinely novel part SLSA lacks).
